decisions.reason: Report names the dsh web host node.exe PID 42432 from running-processes.txt as the koffi.node holder, explains the loaded native binary stays locked until that host exits so npm's copyfile fails with EBUSY, and correctly marks the npm process as victim not holder.

Report states a refresh only reloads the SPA while the lock-owning host process stays alive, then gives an ordered procedure: fully stop the dsh host (and worker), verify via tasklist that no dsh-related node.exe remains, install, then restart and verify. Killing is scoped to dsh processes, not every unrelated Node process.

Report explains an unpinned global install resolves the bare name against the default latest dist-tag instead of preserving or advancing the installed version, cites npm-dist-tags.txt showing latest/next at 0.1.1-rc.2 and alpha at 0.1.2-alpha.5, and concludes alpha.4 was silently replaced by the older rc.2.

Section 3 gives the exact pinned combined command installing dsh@0.1.2-alpha.5 plus the TUI plugin after stopping the host, requires verifying dsh --version prints alpha.5 before restart, and restarts the host. The @alpha tag appears only as a discussed mutable alternative, not as a replacement for the exact pin.

Prevention section tells authors to never ship an unpinned host package name, pin the exact tested core version whenever a plugin command also installs dsh, pin or split combined commands, and warns that tag-following silently drifts to latest; the quoted unpinned command is presented as the bad pattern, not endorsed.
